title: The Fisherman and the Little Fish
text:
A fisherman who lived on what his nets brought in had a bad day. After hours of work he pulled in his net and found only one fish in it, and a very small one at that.

The little fish gasped and flapped and begged for its life. What use was it to him? It was hardly a mouthful. It was not yet grown. If he would only throw it back into the sea, it would soon grow into a big fish, fit for the tables of rich people. Then he could come back, catch it again, and sell it for a good price.

The fisherman listened and then shook his head. He would be a fool, he said, to give up a gain he had in his hand for the hope of a bigger one that might never come. The sea was wide and the fish might swim anywhere, or be caught by someone else, or never be seen again.

He put the little fish in his basket and took it home.
lesson: Weigh a certain small gain against an uncertain larger one honestly. Promises of more later, especially from someone who wants to escape, are worth less than what is already in your hands.
